_README: Hand-set expected pronunciations, ARPAbet, highest precedence of all
reference layers. Use for items where the dictionary is absent or wrong,
or where the study teaches one particular form.
Format:  "word": "PH ON ES"   or   "word": ["FORM ONE", "FORM TWO"]
Several forms are all ACCEPTED - scoring keeps the best-matching one.
Edit and restart, or call references.reload_sources().
Entries here are scored without question, so they should be signed off by
whoever decides what the study teaches.
_why_niche: BEEP gives only 'N IH CH' (the anglicised 'nitch'). British and Kenyan English overwhelmingly use the French-derived /ni:S/ 'neesh', which is what the study recordings contain. Scoring against 'nitch' marked correct speech wrong AND made the robot name CH as the sound to fix - telling the participant to correct the one thing they had right. Both forms are accepted; 'neesh' is listed first as the taught form.
_why_colonel: BEEP is right (/k3:n@l/, 'KER-nl') and needs no override; this note records that the ITEM PROMPT is wrong. It teaches 'Listen CO-LO-NEL. Now you try saying CO-LO-NEL', a three-syllable spelling pronunciation that is not the word. A participant who follows the robot will be marked wrong by a correctly-working scorer. Fix the prompt, not the reference.
_why_worcestershire: Left to the lexicon deliberately. The prompt teaches 'WUSS-ter-sher', which the CMU_ADAPTED entry already covers via its SH AH variant.
_why_tuktuk: Kenyan English, absent from BEEP and CMUdict. g2p predicted 'T AH1 T K AH0' (roughly 'tutka'), which failed both study attempts on a reference error rather than a pronunciation error.
tuktuk: T UH K T UH K
T AH K T AH K
_why_quinoa: Absent from BEEP. g2p gave 'K W IH1 N OW0' (kwih-noh), but the robot's own prompt teaches 'keen-waa'. Scoring against a form the participant was never taught is not a pronunciation test.
quinoa: K W IY N OW AH
_why_comparable: Two standard stress patterns exist: the traditional COM-parable (BEEP: K AA M P AH R AH B L) and the now-common com-PAR-able (/k@m'par@bl/). BEEP lists only the first. Both are accepted; BEEP's form is listed first so the robot keeps modelling the traditional one. Note the 2026-09-15 pilot attempts at this word were heard as 'comfortable' (K AH M F ER T AH B AH L) - a different word, correctly failed - so this entry fixes the reference, not those attempts.
comparable: K AA M P AH R AH B L
K AH M P AE R AH B L
K AH M P EH R AH B L
_why_rendezvous: BEEP and CMUdict both give only the reduced second vowel (R AA/AO N D IH V UW, 'ron-di-voo'). The Longman Pronunciation Dictionary's British form is /'rOndeIvu:/ with a full DEY, which is what both 2026-09-15 pilot attempts contained (heard R AO N D EY V UW) and were failed for. Both are accepted; the DEY form is listed first as the taught form. Final Z (plural/verb) stays as an accepted variant.
rendezvous: R AO N D EY V UW
R AA N D EY V UW
R AO N D IH V UW
R AA N D IH V UW
R AO N D EY V UW Z

bodaboda: B OW D AH B OW D AH
matatu: M AH T AA T UW
